rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the provision found with Mary as knowledge.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه قال رزقا أي علما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an inward reading, Imran's wife represents the soul at the first stage of obeying the intellect.
rows.anchor: وهي النفس في أول مراتب طاعتها لعمران العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The child vowed in the womb symbolizes the heart, represented as a boy; being freed means owing no servitude to created things.
rows.anchor: محررا ) ليس في رق شئ من المخلوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The female symbolizes a soul too, but one more advanced in rank; like reproduces like.
rows.anchor: وهي نفس ايضا إلا أنها أكمل منها في المرتبة والجنس يلد الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what she has borne because this woman will manifest extraordinary marvels, while no secret is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: لعلمه أنه سيظهر من هذه الأنثى العجب العجاب وغيره سبحانه تخفي عليه الأسرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maryam signifies the worshipper; Satan and the requested protection from him signify carnal desires veiling the sanctified soul from the gardens of the spiritual kingdom.
rows.anchor: وهو الشهوات النفسانية الحاجبة للنفس القدسية عن رياض الملكوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's good acceptance represents His choosing Mary for the outpouring of His lights.
rows.anchor: وهو اختصاصه إياها بإفاضة أنواره عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her good growth is a pure ascent through the stages of completion, unimpeded by obstacles or attachments.
rows.anchor: ورقاها فيما تكمل به نشأتها ترقيا حسنا غير مشوب بالعوائق والعلائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya symbolizes spiritual preparedness.
rows.anchor: الاستعداد ( كلما دخل عليها زكريا ) وتوجه نحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya's entering represents turning toward her in her worship niche, built in the heart's sanctified house.
rows.anchor: في محراب تعبدها المبني لها في بيت مقدس القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The provision is nourishment for spirits in the realm of the unseen dominion.
rows.anchor: تتغذى به الأرواح في عالم الملكوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's answer means the great provision flows from God, beyond the reach of intellectual thought.
rows.anchor: هو مفاض من عند الله منزه عن الحمل بيد الافكار

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gathers the attributes of beauty and majesty, bestows knowledge according to each recipient's capacity, and gives without measure.
rows.anchor: الجامع لصفات الجمال والجلال ( يرزق من يشاء ) ويفيض عليهم من علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That points back to the remarkable preceding accounts, which are hidden from the Prophet and his people and knowable only through revelation.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما تقدم ذكره من تلك الاخبار البديعة الشأن المرتقية من الغرابة إلى أعلى مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That is the subject, with from the unseen reports as its predicate; the sentence is grammatically independent.
rows.anchor: وهو مبتدأ خبره قوله تعالى : ( من أنبآء الغيب ( أي من أخبار ما غاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause from the unseen reports is an independent sentence with no grammatical position.
rows.anchor: والجملة مستأنفة لا محل لها من الاعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation is imparting meaning secretly; the word can also mean an angel's delivery to prophets or inspiration.
rows.anchor: إلقاء المعنى إلى الغير على وجه خفي ويكون بمعنى إرسال الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most take its pronoun to refer to that; al-Alusi prefers the unseen, which includes both previously told and untold stories.
rows.anchor: عائد إلى ذلك في المشهور واستحسن عوده إلى الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate parsing makes this clause the predicate, with from the unseen reports attached to the verb or circumstantial from its object; some make it circumstantial from the subject.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن تكون هذه الجملة خبرا عن المبتدأ قبلها

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa proposes an omitted subject meaning the matter is that, with the prepositional phrase circumstantial; al-Alusi rejects this as unworthy of the divine speech.
rows.anchor: التقدير الامر ( ذلك ) فيكون ( ذلك ) خبرا لمبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some take the present tense to signal that revelation was still continuing.
rows.anchor: وصيغة الاستقبال عند قوم للإيذان بأن الوحي لم ينقطع بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unstated pronoun means those disputing over Mary, inferred from the context.
rows.anchor: أي عند المتنازعين فالضمير عائد إلى غير مذكور دل عليه المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of the Prophet's presence establishes that his account came by revelation: reason and prior reading or hearing could not supply it, leaving only impossible eyewitnessing.
rows.anchor: تحقيق كون الاخبار بما ذكر عن وحي على سبيل التهكم بمنكريه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's story is foregrounded although Zakariya's story was also revealed, because Mary is the primary subject; Zakariya's account enters incidentally and is partly implied by the mention of her caretaker.
rows.anchor: هي المقصودة بالاخبار أولا وإنما جاءت القصة الأخرى على سبيل الاستطراد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the sentence marvels at the people's eagerness to take responsibility for Mary and reinforces her selection.
rows.anchor: وروى عن قتادة أن المقصود من هذه الجملة تعجيب الله سبحانه نبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi finds Qatada's reading strained because it separates emphasis from what is emphasized, yet prefers it to the alternative explanation.
rows.anchor: ويبعد هذا الفصل بين المؤكد والمؤكد ومع هذا هو أولى مما قيل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An alternative says the verse marvels that people shirked Mary's care because of their hardship and need until Zakariya became her excellent guardian; al-Alusi nearly rejects this as unsound in reason and transmission.
rows.anchor: إن المقصود منها التعجيب من تدافعهم لكفالتها لشدة الحال ومزيد الحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whichever purpose is adopted, denying eyewitnessing poses no problem because its impossibility is evident to everyone.
rows.anchor: لا يشكل نفي المشاهدة مع ظهور انتقائها عند كل أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pens are cast or thrown for drawing lots; qalam is the plural of pen.
rows.anchor: يرمونها ويطرحونها للاقتراع و الاقلام جمع قلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lots used their Torah-writing pens, chosen for the blessing associated with them.
rows.anchor: وهي التي كانوا يكتبون بها التوراة واختاروها تبركا بها

rows.speaker: الكازروني
rows.claim: Others say the lots were arrows or divining shafts; al-Kazruni reports that they were made of copper.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي السهام من النشاب وهي القداح وحكى الكازروني أنها كانت من نحاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qalam derives from a root meaning to cut, as in a nail clipping.
rows.anchor: وهي مأخوذة من القلم بمعنى القطع ومنه قلامة الظفر

rows.speaker: الباقر
rows.claim: Al-Baqir says the number of lots was six; the source notes disagreement about their number.
rows.anchor: وفي عدة الأقلام خلاف وعن الباقر أنها كانت ستة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporal clause is governed by the existential construction operating in with them.
rows.anchor: والظرف معمول للاستقرار العامل في ( لديهم ) وجعله ظرفا

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa's alternative attachment of the time phrase to كان is rejected.
rows.anchor: وجعله ظرفا لكان كما قال أبو البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Who will care for Mary continues the preceding construction; treating it as a fresh direct question corrupts the meaning.
rows.anchor: من تتمة الكلام الأول وجعله ابتداء استفهام مفسد للمعنى

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب وابن مالك
rows.claim: One proposed ellipsis is they look to see who will care for Mary; looking can govern an interrogative like a verb of cognition, as Ibn al-Hajib and Ibn Malik state.
rows.anchor: أن يقدر ينظرون ( أيهم يكفل ) وحيث كان النظر مما يؤدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second ellipsis supplies they may know who will care for Mary; the clause is purposive, although casting lots is only an indirect cause and observing which pen rises is the immediate cause.
rows.anchor: أن يقدر ليعلموا ( أيهم يكفل ) وعلى الأول الجملة حال مما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third proposal supplies they say or so they say; critics find it purposeless, while its defenders understand saying as identifying or judging who will care for her.
rows.anchor: أن يقدر يقولون أو ليقولوا ( أيهم ) واعترض بأنه لا فائدة يعتد بها

rows.speaker: السكاكي
rows.claim: Al-Sakkaki supplies they look so they may know, perhaps to preserve both the sense and wording; either verb of looking or knowing could suffice.
rows.anchor: والسكاكي يقدر ههنا ينظرون ليعلموا ولعل ذلك لمراعاة المعنى واللفظ

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some exacting scholars supply no omitted verb and make who will care for Mary an appositive to the plural pronoun, a strained analysis.
rows.anchor: وبعض المحققين لم يقدر شيئا أصلا وجعل ( أيهم ) بدلا عن ضمير الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispute concerned competing over Mary's guardianship; one view places it after the lot drawing and another before it.
rows.anchor: في شأنها تنافسا على كفالتها وكان هذا الاختصام بعد الاقتراع في رأي وقبله في آخر

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: Repeating that the Prophet was not present makes each absence an independent proof of prophethood; the altered order of events in the second account strengthens the point.
rows.anchor: للايذان بأن كل واحد من عدم الحضور عند الإلقاء وعدم الحضور عند الاختصام مستقل بالشهادة على نبوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well-known, relied-upon view places the drawing of lots when Mary was born and her mother brought her to the church; another weak view places it when grown Mary became difficult for Zakariya to raise, and a still weaker view says it happened twice.
rows.anchor: أحدهما وهو المشهور المعول عليه أنه كان حين ولادتها وحمل أمها لها إلى الكنيسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that drawing lots can help determine disputed rights.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أن القرعة لها دخل في تمييز الحقوق

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says that people who cast lots while entrusting the matter to God see the rightful claimant's lot succeed, and cites the lot cast by Jonah.
rows.anchor: وروى عن الصادق رضى الله تعالى عنه أنه قال

rows.speaker: الباقر
rows.claim: Al-Baqir says Mary daughter of Imran was the first person against whom lots were cast, citing this verse.
rows.anchor: وقال الباقر رضي الله تعالى عنه : أول من سوهم عليه مريم بنت عمران

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the two scriptural communities disputed before the Prophet over which followed Abraham; when he said neither did, they angrily rejected his judgment and religion, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: اختصم أهل الكتابين إلى رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فيما اختلفوا بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence may coordinate with the combined condition and result, or with the result alone; the latter permits an independent interrogative to follow a statement here.
rows.anchor: والجملة في النظم معطوفة على مجموع الشرط والجزاء وقيل : على الجزاء فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either syntactic analysis, the interrogative hamza falls between the coordinated elements to express rejection.
rows.anchor: والهمزة على التقديرين متوسطة بين المعطوف والمعطوف عليه للانكار

rows.speaker: سيبويه والجمهور
rows.claim: Sibawayh and most grammarians posit an omitted question such as do they turn away, followed by so do they seek; Ibn Hisham calls this the primary analysis and al-Zamakhshari affirms it in several places.
rows.anchor: قال ابن هشام : والاول مذهب سيبويه والجمهور

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham allows in some places a second analysis connecting the question directly to the preceding sentence, but the source finds this strained and not generally applicable.
rows.anchor: وجوز الثاني في بعض ويضعفه ما فيه من التكلف

rows.speaker: الشمس بن الصائغ
rows.claim: Al-Shams ibn al-Saigh counters that an omitted question can be supplied in the verse about the One who watches every soul, as a rhetorical affirmation of the Creator.
rows.anchor: وتعقبه الشمس بن الصائغ بأنهأي مانع من تقدير ألا مدبر للموجودات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says to supply an omitted clause only when it naturally comes to mind; otherwise he follows the grammarians who take the sentence as coordinated without one.
rows.anchor: إن انساق ذلك المقدر للذهن قيل : بالتقدير وإلا قيل : بما قاله الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object is fronted because it is the focus of rejection, not to claim exclusivity; the rejected act is seeking a religion other than God's.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المفعول لأنه المقصود بالانكار لا للحصر كما توهم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says fronting reflects looseness in expression and resemblance to the verse ending; al-Alusi says this explanation has no merit among careful scholars.
rows.anchor: إن تعليل التقديم بما تقدم لا تحقيق فيه لأن الانكار الذي هو معنى الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Amr, Hafs from Asim, and Yaqub read in the third person; the rest read in the second person, with an implied do you turn away, act impiously, or disbelieve, while some call it a shift of person.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وعاصم في رواية لحفص ويعقوب يبغون بالياء التحتية وقرأ الباقون بالتاء الفوقانية

words: وَلَهُۥٓ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause that all in the heavens and earth submit to Him is circumstantial and reinforces the rejection: how can they seek another religion in that state?
rows.anchor: جملة حالية مؤكدة للانكار أي كيف يبغون ويطلبون غير دينه والحالة هذه

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: The two adverbs are circumstantial verbal nouns meaning willingly and unwillingly; Abu al-Baqa also treats them as verbal nouns for submission or obedience, though the source questions how that fits unwillingly.
rows.anchor: مصدران في موضع الحال أي طائعين وكارهين وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكونا مصدرين على غير المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes willing submission as faith gained through knowledge, by reasoning or without reflection, and unwilling submission as Islam imposed by the sword or coercion.
rows.anchor: المراد من الاسلام بالطوع الاسلام الناشي عن العلم مطلقا سواء كان حاصلا للاستدلال

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reading says angels and believers obey willingly, while disbelievers are subject to God's will even in their disbelief; this does not entail determinism, erase their accountability, or collapse the distinction between believer and unbeliever.
rows.anchor: انقادوا له تعالى مختارين لامره كالملائكة والمؤمنين مسخرين لارادته كالكفرة

rows.speaker: بعض ساداتنا الصوفية
rows.claim: Sufi authorities distinguish willing submission without carnal darkness or ego veils from unwilling submission amid inner resistance, whispers, veils, and attachment to intermediaries.
rows.anchor: الاسلام طوعا هو الانقياد والامتثال لما أمر الله تعالى من غير معارضة ظلمة نفسانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sufi account exemplifies the first state in angels and some elect people, and the second in many people who waver among religious schools without finding certainty, as the quoted poem illustrates.
rows.anchor: فلم أر إلا واضعا كف حائر على ذقن أو قارعا سن نادم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelievers belong to the second class because they acknowledge a creator but their self-darkness prevents recognition of truth; the cited verses express that admission and their continued associationism.
rows.anchor: لانهم أثبتوا صانعا أيضا إلا أن ظلمة أنفسهم حالت بينهم وبين الوقوف على الحق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says Mujahid's words point toward the Sufi account of the two kinds of submission.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا يشير كلام مجاهد

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliyah says every person acknowledges God as Lord and self as servant; associating in worship is submission under compulsion, while sincere devotion is willing submission.
rows.anchor: عن أبي العالية أنه قال

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-A'mash reads the word for unwillingly with a damma on its first consonant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش كرها بالضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: According to the well-known view, all return to God for recompense, so they should hasten to His religion and not oppose Islam.
rows.anchor: أي إلى جزائه تصيرون على المشهور فبادروا إلى دينه ولا تخالفوا الاسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return clause may stand independently as a threat or coordinate with all submit to Him as another circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: وجوزوا في الجملة أن تكون مستأنفة للاخبار بما تضمنته من التهديد وأن تكون معطوفة على ( وله أسلم )

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Asim reads the return verb in the third person; its pronoun refers either to all who are in the heavens and earth or to those seeking another religion, with a person shift in the latter reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم بياء الغيبة والضمير لمن أو لمن عاد اليه

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use the second person, with the pronoun returning to the people denoted by the subject of seeking; if the earlier verb is third person, this too creates a shift in person.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالخطاب والضمير عائد لمن عاد اليه

rows.speaker: طاوس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Tawus and Mujahid say God lightens the rules about women and marriage by permitting marriage to enslaved women; al-Alusi's later contextual argument supports this reading.
rows.anchor: أي في التكليف في أمر النساء والنكاح بإباحة نكاح الإماء قاله طاوس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view takes the easing generally: God lightened obligations for this community compared with earlier communities.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يخفف في التكليف على العموم فإنه تعالى خفف عن هذه الأمة ما لم يخفف عن غيرها

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A further view says God eases matters by accepting repentance and enabling people to repent.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يخفف بقبول التوبة والتوفيق لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is independent and has no grammatical position in what precedes.
rows.anchor: والجملة مستأنفة لا محل لها من الإعراب

rows.speaker: طاوس
rows.claim: Tawus says human weakness here concerns women: a man cannot patiently abstain from them.
rows.anchor: أي في أمر النساء لا يصبر عنهن قاله طاوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report says there is no good in women and no patience without them: they overcome a noble man, while a noble man does not overcome them, and the speaker prefers being nobly overcome.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر لا خير في النساء ولا صبر عنهن يغلبن كريما ويغلبهن لئيم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Other explanations say desire sways a person, fear and grief unsettle him, or he cannot oppose appetite and bear the hardship of obedience.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يستميله هواه وشهوته ويستشيطه خوفه وحزنه وقيل : عاجز عن مخالفة الهوى وتحمل مشاق الطاعة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view calls people weak in judgment: only divine light lets them discern hidden secrets and wisdom.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ضعيف الرأي لا يدرك الأسرار والحكم إلا بنور إلهي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the weakness is physical: even a small event causes pain; al-Alusi rejects this and weak judgment as poorly supported by the context, which concerns the marriage dispensation.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن رضي الله تعالى عنه أن المراد ضعيف الخلقة يؤلمه أدنى حادث نزل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weak is parsed as an accusative circumstantial, or as if a preposition meaning from had been omitted before weak.
rows.anchor: ونصب ضعيفا على الحال وقيل : على نزع الخافض أي من ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative construed as created from a weak substance, whether clay or semen, does not fit the context.
rows.anchor: وأريد به الطين أو النطفة وكلاهما كما ترى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the verb actively, with God as its subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ( وخلق الإنسان ) على البناء للفاعل والضمير لله عز وجل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi reports Ibn Abbas saying that eight verses in Surat al-Nisa are better for this community than all that the sun rises and sets upon, listing 4:26, 4:27, 4:28, 4:31, 4:40, 4:110, 4:48, and 4:152.
rows.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي في الشعب عنه أنه قال : ثماني آيات نزلت في سورة النساء هي خير لهذه الأمة

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: Qatada recounts that Banu Ubayriq were a poor family; Bishr was a hypocritical poet who composed insults against the Companions and falsely attributed them to others.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة بن النعمان رضى الله تعالى عنه أنه قال : كان أهل بيت منا

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: Qatada says his uncle Rifa'a stored flour, weapons, and supplies in a room; the room was broken into at night, and the flour and weapons were stolen.
rows.anchor: فابتاع عمى رفاعة بن زيد حملا من الدرمك فجعله فى مشربة له

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: The family suspected Banu Ubayriq after seeing their fire, but they blamed the upright Muslim Lubayd; he drew his sword and demanded they identify the thief.
rows.anchor: قد رأينا بنى أبيرق قد استوقدوا فى هذه الليلة ولانرى فيما نرى إلا على بعض طعامكم

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: Qatada sought the Prophet's help recovering the weapons, not the food; the Ubayriq family rallied Usayr ibn Urwa and neighbors, who accused Qatada and his uncle of slandering pious Muslims without proof.
rows.anchor: فأتيت رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه و سلم ) فقلت : يارسول الله إن أهل بيت منا أهل جفاء

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: Qatada says the Prophet rebuked him for accusing a devout household without evidence; after revelation, the Prophet returned the weapon, and Rifa'a affirmed his sincere faith by dedicating it to God's cause.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : فأتيت رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه و سلم ) فكلمته فقال

rows.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
rows.claim: Hassan ibn Thabit satirized Sulafa for sheltering the fugitive Bashir; after hearing the poem, she threw his belongings at al-Abtah and complained that he brought her nothing but trouble.
rows.anchor: إن حسان بن ثابت رضى الله تعالى عنه هجا سلافة فقال

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi's alternative account, preferred by al-Tabari, says a Jew entrusted armor to Ta'ma ibn Ubayriq; Ta'ma stole it, hid it in Abu Malik's house, accused Abu Malik, and asked the Prophet to defend him against the Jews, just before revelation exposed the theft.
rows.anchor: عن السدي واختاره الطبري أن يهوديا استودع طعمة بن أبيرق درعا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: In al-Suddi's account Ta'ma fled to Mecca as an apostate after exposure, tried to rob his host al-Hajjaj ibn Ilat, was expelled, and died as an unbeliever at Banu Sulaym's lava field.
rows.anchor: فلما فضح الله تعالى طعمة بالقرآن هرب حتى أتى مكة فكفر بعد إسلامه

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima gives another fate: a stone struck Ta'ma while he tried to rob al-Hajjaj; later, after he robbed a Quda'a caravan, its members caught and stoned him to death.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة أن طعمه لما نزل فيه القرآن ولحق بقريش ورجع عن دينه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says Ta'ma died when a house he broke into in Mecca collapsed on him.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن زيد أنه بعد أن لحق بمكة نقب بيتا يسرقه فهدمه الله تعالى عليه فقتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another version says Ta'ma was expelled, sailed to Jeddah, stole a purse of dinars aboard ship, and was caught and thrown into the sea.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنه أخرج فركب سفينة إلى جدة فسرق فيها كيسا فيه دنانير فأخذ وألقى في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Emphasis signals the ruling's importance; ascribing revelation to the majestic first-person plural magnifies it, and fronting the object draws attention and anticipation.
rows.anchor: في تأكيد الحكم إيذان بالاعتناء بشأنه كما فى إسناد الانزال إلى ضمير العظمة تعظيما لأمر المسند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With truth is a circumstantial phrase: God sent the Qur'an down in a state of truth.
rows.anchor: وقوله سبحانه : بالحق فى موضع الحال أى إنا أنزلنا اليك القرآن متلبسا بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to judge all people, upright and wicked alike.
rows.anchor: متلبسا بالحق ( لتحكم بين الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God showed you means what He made known and revealed to you.
rows.anchor: بما عرفك وأوحى به اليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun has an omitted referent and is the first object of araka; the verb comes from ra'a meaning to know, normally one-object but causativized here to two.
rows.anchor: و ( ما موصولة والعائد محذوف وهو المفعول الأول لأرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking the verb as opinion, like al-Shafi'i held this, would make it a cognitive verb needing three objects with two omitted; al-Alusi calls this remote, and a metaphorical inner sight is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنها من الرأى من قولهم : رأى الشافعى كذا وجعلها علمية يقتضى التعدى إلى ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The traitors are the Banu Ubayriq or Ta'ma, the person intended by the warning, or anyone who follows their conduct.
rows.anchor: وهم بنو أبيرق أوطعمة ومن يعنيه أو هو ومن يسير بسيرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition can mean for their sake, or alternatively away from or concerning them.
rows.anchor: واللام للتعليل وقيل : بمعنى عن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An advocate here means someone arguing against innocent people.
rows.anchor: أى مخاصما للبرآء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition most naturally follows an omitted command to judge by the Book; alternatives coordinate it with We sent down by supplying We said, or with the Book because the prohibition was also revealed, but the latter is far from the apparent construction.
rows.anchor: والنهى معطوف على مقدر ينسحب عليه النظم الكريم كأنه قيل : إنا أنزلنا اليك الكتاب فاحكم به
